+/// What a key means for the `?` help overlay. One shared rule for every
+/// attach surface: `?` opens, any key while open closes, everything else
+/// flows through to the surface's normal handling.
+#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
+pub(crate) enum HelpKeyAction {
+    Open,
+    Close,
+    NotHandled,
+}
+
+pub(crate) fn handle_help_key(help_open: bool, key: KeyEvent) -> HelpKeyAction {
+    if help_open {
+        return HelpKeyAction::Close;
+    }
+    if key.code == KeyCode::Char('?') {
+        return HelpKeyAction::Open;
+    }
+    HelpKeyAction::NotHandled
+}
+
 /// Route `key` through the shared navigation keys, falling back to the surface's
 /// mode-specific hook. Returns `true` if the key was handled.
 pub(crate) fn dispatch_navigation<S: NavigableSurface + ?Sized>(

+            KeyCode::Char('?'),

+            assert_eq!(
+                handle_help_key(true, key(code)),
+                HelpKeyAction::Close,
+                "{code:?} must close the open overlay instead of acting"
+            );
+        }
+        assert_eq!(
+            handle_help_key(false, key(KeyCode::Char('q'))),
+            HelpKeyAction::NotHandled
+        );
+    }

+/// Which attach surface the `?` help overlay describes. Uniform chrome,
+/// mode-specific content: every surface gets the same overlay frame and close
+/// semantics, with only the binding list varying.
+#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
+pub(crate) enum AttachHelpMode {
+    Run,
+    Plan,
+    Campaign,
+    Chain,
+}
+
+impl AttachHelpMode {
+    fn title(self) -> &'static str {
+        match self {
+            Self::Run => "run attach keys",
+            Self::Plan => "plan attach keys",
+            Self::Campaign => "campaign attach keys",
+            Self::Chain => "chain attach keys",
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+/// The complete binding list per attach surface — the footer shows the
+/// load-bearing subset and truncates on narrow terminals; this overlay is the
+/// full reference, one keystroke away.
+pub(crate) fn help_overlay_lines(mode: AttachHelpMode) -> Vec<(&'static str, &'static str)> {
+    match mode {
+        AttachHelpMode::Run => vec![
+            ("q / Esc / Ctrl-D", "detach (run keeps going)"),
+            ("b / Backspace", "back to plan (when drilled in)"),
+            ("n", "toggle narrative / activity panels"),
+            ("v", "cycle visual map mode (narrative view)"),
+            ("r", "refresh narrative"),
+            ("Tab / Shift-Tab", "switch focused panel"),
+            ("j k / Up Down", "scroll focused panel"),
+            ("PgUp / PgDn", "page"),
+            ("Home End / g G", "jump to start / end"),
+            ("c", "open chain context (chain-step runs)"),
+            ("a", "apply completed run (y confirms)"),
+            ("x", "abandon completed run (y confirms)"),
+            ("m / e", "materialize / extend completed run"),
+            ("s / d", "show details / toggle docs"),
+            ("?", "toggle this help"),
+        ],
+        AttachHelpMode::Plan => vec![
+            ("q / Esc / Ctrl-D", "detach (plan keeps going)"),
+            ("b / Backspace", "back to campaign (when drilled in)"),
+            ("Enter", "open the selected child run"),
+            ("n", "toggle narrative / task cards"),
+            ("v", "cycle visual map mode (narrative view)"),
+            ("r", "refresh narrative"),
+            ("j k / Up Down", "select task / scroll narrative"),
+            ("PgUp / PgDn", "page"),
+            ("Home End / g G", "jump to start / end"),
+            ("?", "toggle this help"),
+        ],
+        AttachHelpMode::Campaign => vec![
+            ("q / Ctrl-D", "detach (campaign keeps going)"),
+            ("b / Esc / Backspace", "back"),
+            ("Enter", "drill into the selected sub-plan"),
+            ("r", "refresh"),
+            ("j k / Up Down / Tab", "select sub-plan"),
+            ("PgUp / PgDn", "page"),
+            ("Home End / g G", "jump to start / end"),
+            ("?", "toggle this help"),
+        ],
+        AttachHelpMode::Chain => vec![
+            ("q / Esc / Ctrl-D", "detach (chain keeps going)"),
+            ("Enter", "show the selected step's run"),
+            ("r", "redo the selected step"),
+            ("e", "extend the chain with a new step"),
+            ("p", "pause the chain"),
+            ("k", "kill the chain (asks to confirm)"),
+            ("Up / Down", "select step"),
+            ("PgUp / PgDn", "scroll activity"),
+            ("?", "toggle this help"),
+        ],
+    }
+}
+
+/// Draw the `?` help overlay: a centered popup over the current frame. Any
+/// key closes it.
+pub(crate) fn render_help_overlay(frame: &mut ratatui::Frame<'_>, mode: AttachHelpMode) {
+    let lines = help_overlay_lines(mode);
+    let key_width = lines
+        .iter()
+        .map(|(key, _)| key.len())
+        .max()
+        .unwrap_or(0);
+    let body: Vec<Line<'static>> = lines
+        .iter()
+        .map(|(key, action)| {
+            Line::from(vec![
+                Span::styled(
+                    format!(" {key:key_width$}  "),
+                    Style::default()
+                        .fg(Color::Cyan)
+                        .add_modifier(Modifier::BOLD),
+                ),
+                Span::raw((*action).to_string()),
+            ])
+        })
+        .collect();
+    let width = (key_width + 44).min(frame.area().width.saturating_sub(2) as usize) as u16;
+    let height = (body.len() as u16 + 2).min(frame.area().height.saturating_sub(2));
+    let area = centered_rect(frame.area(), width.max(20), height.max(3));
+    frame.render_widget(Clear, area);
+    frame.render_widget(
+        Paragraph::new(body).block(
+            Block::default()
+                .borders(Borders::ALL)
+                .title(format!("{} — any key closes", mode.title())),
+        ),
+        area,
+    );
+}
+
+fn centered_rect(
+    outer: ratatui::layout::Rect,
+    width: u16,
+    height: u16,
+) -> ratatui::layout::Rect {
+    let width = width.min(outer.width);
+    let height = height.min(outer.height);
+    ratatui::layout::Rect {
+        x: outer.x + (outer.width.saturating_sub(width)) / 2,
+        y: outer.y + (outer.height.saturating_sub(height)) / 2,
+        width,
+        height,
+    }
+}
+

     turn_label: &str,

+#[test]
+fn help_overlay_lists_complete_bindings_per_mode() {
+    for mode in [
+        AttachHelpMode::Run,
+        AttachHelpMode::Plan,
+        AttachHelpMode::Campaign,
+        AttachHelpMode::Chain,
+    ] {
+        let lines = help_overlay_lines(mode);
+        let keys = lines.iter().map(|(key, _)| *key).collect::<Vec<_>>();
+        assert!(
+            keys.iter().any(|key| key.contains('q')),
+            "{mode:?} must document detach"
+        );
+        assert_eq!(
+            keys.last().copied(),
+            Some("?"),
+            "{mode:?} must document the help toggle itself"
+        );
+        let actions = lines.iter().map(|(_, action)| *action).collect::<Vec<_>>();
+        assert!(
+            actions.iter().all(|action| !action.is_empty()),
+            "{mode:?} has an unlabeled key"
+        );
+    }
+
+    // One keymap: abandon is x (with confirm) in run attach, and the chain
+    // surface documents that k means kill, not scroll.
+    let run = help_overlay_lines(AttachHelpMode::Run);
+    assert!(
+        run.iter()
+            .any(|(key, action)| *key == "x" && action.contains("abandon")),
+        "run overlay must document x abandon"
+    );
+    let chain = help_overlay_lines(AttachHelpMode::Chain);
+    assert!(
+        chain
+            .iter()
+            .any(|(key, action)| *key == "k" && action.contains("kill")),
+        "chain overlay must document k kill"
+    );
+}
+

1	use crossterm::event::{KeyCode, KeyEvent};

3	/// Shared navigation core for every attach surface (run, plan, campaign, chain).
4	///
5	/// The run panel's key semantics are the reference. Each surface implements the
6	/// movement hooks for its own content model (multi-panel scroll, list selection,
7	/// step graph, …) and supplies `mode_key` for its mode-specific keys. The common
8	/// navigation keys — arrows/`jk`, `Tab`/`BackTab`, `PgUp`/`PgDn`, `Home`/`End`,
9	/// `g`/`G` — are routed identically for everyone by [`dispatch_navigation`].
10	pub(crate) trait NavigableSurface {
11	    /// `Tab`: move focus to the next panel (no-op for single-panel surfaces).
12	    fn focus_next(&mut self) {}
13	    /// `BackTab`: move focus to the previous panel.
14	    fn focus_previous(&mut self) {}
15	    /// `Up`/`k` (delta -1) and `Down`/`j` (delta +1).
16	    fn scroll_lines(&mut self, delta: isize);
17	    /// `PgUp` (direction -1) and `PgDn` (direction +1).
18	    fn scroll_page(&mut self, direction: isize);
19	    /// `Home`/`g`.
20	    fn scroll_to_start(&mut self);
21	    /// `End`/`G`.
22	    fn scroll_to_end(&mut self);
23	    /// Handle a key the shared core does not own. Return `true` if consumed.
24	    fn mode_key(&mut self, _key: KeyEvent) -> bool {
25	        false
26	    }
27	}
28	
29	/// What a key means for the `?` help overlay. One shared rule for every
30	/// attach surface: `?` opens, any key while open closes, everything else
31	/// flows through to the surface's normal handling.
32	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
33	pub(crate) enum HelpKeyAction {
34	    Open,
35	    Close,
36	    NotHandled,
37	}
38	
39	pub(crate) fn handle_help_key(help_open: bool, key: KeyEvent) -> HelpKeyAction {
40	    if help_open {
41	        return HelpKeyAction::Close;
42	    }
43	    if key.code == KeyCode::Char('?') {
44	        return HelpKeyAction::Open;
45	    }
46	    HelpKeyAction::NotHandled
47	}
48	
49	/// Route `key` through the shared navigation keys, falling back to the surface's
50	/// mode-specific hook. Returns `true` if the key was handled.
51	pub(crate) fn dispatch_navigation<S: NavigableSurface + ?Sized>(
52	    surface: &mut S,
53	    key: KeyEvent,
54	) -> bool {
55	    match key.code {
56	        KeyCode::Tab => surface.focus_next(),
57	        KeyCode::BackTab => surface.focus_previous(),
58	        KeyCode::Up | KeyCode::Char('k') => surface.scroll_lines(-1),
59	        KeyCode::Down | KeyCode::Char('j') => surface.scroll_lines(1),
60	        KeyCode::PageUp => surface.scroll_page(-1),
61	        KeyCode::PageDown => surface.scroll_page(1),
62	        KeyCode::Home | KeyCode::Char('g') => surface.scroll_to_start(),
63	        KeyCode::End | KeyCode::Char('G') => surface.scroll_to_end(),
64	        _ => return surface.mode_key(key),
65	    }
66	    true
67	}

I've reviewed the diff. This change is exclusively a TUI help-overlay feature plus a single CLI-prompt keymap rename:

**What changed**
- `tui/navigation.rs`: new pure function `handle_help_key` — input is a `KeyEvent` struct from `crossterm`, output is an enum; no I/O, no external sources.
- `tui/render.rs`: new `render_help_overlay` that draws a `Paragraph` of **static `&'static str` constants** from `help_overlay_lines`. No user/file/network data is rendered. Width/height arithmetic uses `.saturating_sub`/`.min` against `frame.area()` u16 bounds — no overflow path.
- `commands/attach.rs`, `commands/chain/mod.rs`: wire the help toggle into the existing terminal event loops. The `event::read()` source is unchanged; the help branch only flips a local `bool` and `continue`s. No new auth/exec/path/HTTP/log sinks.
- `main.rs` `completion_action_from_input`: adds `"x"` as a new alias for `Abandon` while keeping `"b"`. Both pre-existed only as input-keymap aliases in an interactive CLI prompt running with the invoker's own privileges; no privilege boundary, no parser-differential (the consumer is the same `match` arm returning `CompletionAction::Abandon`).
- `tui_tests.rs`: tests only.

**Source → sink check**
- The only data reaching renderers is **static `&'static str`** from a `match` over a closed `AttachHelpMode` enum. No attacker-influenced value enters any render/format/exec sink.
- `event::read()` was already trusted upstream; this change does not relax any prior guard. The "any key closes help" semantics actually swallow potentially destructive keys (e.g. `a` apply, `x` abandon, `k` kill) while the overlay is open — a fail-safe, not a regression.
- The CLI alias change is additive and within a fixed enum; no over-broad grant (the action is the user abandoning their own run via stdin prompt, no auth involved).

**Phase 2c high-miss checks**
- No logging of secrets/PII added.
- No IaC/CI trust changes.
- No allowlist/permission/sanitizer registry touched.
- No control-flow regression (no fail-closed validator deleted).
- No threshold/state security decision added.

No vulnerabilities identified.
